name_reason: Matches fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. domain=chapter_event_handler; descriptor 36=dispatch idx 0x36 (handler-table slot @ table 0x51B91, table entry @ 0x51C69); ch24=chapter 24 (valid chapter domain ID 01-30); cinematic=category. No Ghidra address residue (self addr 0x3535D would be _3535d; absent). All numeric suffixes are meaningful domain IDs, not address residue. Confirmed by table xref and ch24 strategy-guide event (turns 3/4/7/10 enemy reinforcements at 4 corners -> 4-corner establishing pan).
purpose: Chapter 24 cinematic event handler (dispatch idx 0x36): plays the establishing-shot 4-corner camera pan with 400ms holds when enemy reinforcements appear at the map corners; no dialog.
logic_summary: __CHK(0xC) stack-frame guard, then: load the chapter portrait set indexed by the RAW turn counter (data_fd2_battle_turn_counter @ 0x53BEF, no /2 shift) so the set rotates per turn; then four pan_cursor_and_window + 400ms-hold pairs sweeping the map corners: top-left (0,4), bottom-left (0,0x16), bottom-right (0x1A,0x18), top-right (0x1A,2). Returns. In the binary the final pan+hold+RET is a Class-3 shared tail at 0x353C4 (reused by handler_39/ch26), and the 4th delay block at 0x353CC overlaps the separately-registered fd2_delay_400ms_via_idle_thunk callable; both are size optimisations not functional differences.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Per-event dispatch-table ABI argument (event/char id from stack). This handler does not read it (cast to void); it is a no-arg cinematic.
params.reason: Descriptive and consistent with the dispatch-table signature shared across handlers; no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value; runs the cinematic and returns.

notes: Disassembly confirms: PUSH dword ptr [0x53BEF] (RAW turn counter, no shift); 4 pan calls (0,4)/(0,0x16)/(0x1A,0x18)/(0x1A,2) with PUSH 0x190 (=400) delays; PUSH 0xC; CALL 0x36CD7 = __CHK guard; body ends at the 0x353C4 shared-tail boundary. Source comment block (chevt2.c lines 324-345) is already precise and matches disasm + ch24 strategy-guide event; left unchanged. Ghidra plate is consistent (more verbose) with no contradiction; left unchanged. Strategy guide says reinforcement turns 3/4/7/10 vs KB doc 2/4/7/10 -- a trigger-slot vs displayed-turn indexing nuance, not a naming/comment correctness concern.
